meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so I'll be brief. Owen found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, Hale?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.

I'm writing down September 24, 380 words, forty minutes. Put the in-class piece and the essay in front of me, Hale. And you still haven't said who entered the zero, or whether anyone spoke to Owen first.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
Okay. The checker is off the table, and I'm writing that down. Now, what does the version history actually show, and when was it opened?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed in the meeting to take the detector score off the table. I still expect the zero withdrawn, an apology, and the version history put in front of me. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, with the zero withdrawn, an apology and the principal's office still what she wants, since she has seen no document yet.
What moved her: dropping the detector score gave a little ground, because it was the weak point she came prepared to attack, and the dated September 24 comparison made her start writing things down.
What cost ground: leaving unanswered who entered the zero and whether anyone spoke to Owen first, because she asked twice and procedure is what she trusts most.
Try next time: after the September 24 comparison, answer who entered the zero and when you called, own it in one sentence, then put the version history in front of her with its times.
